items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1961-01-29
items.q: And the clarinet player was named Edmund Washington... We all had, we were taking lessons from this, Sam, for the Perkins... Edmund Washington could read, so what we'd do, we'd buy numbers... and run them down.

ctx.x: Where did you go to after Dave Perkins? Did you go to any other teachers?

Well, no. Like I said, this little, this band, they were all fellows older than me because I was just about 18, if I remember well. And they were all the trombone players named George Morris and the trombone players named Thomas Mack. And the clarinet player was named Edmund Washington.

items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1959-01-17
items.q: the band we had when we left here we left here with with Joy Morris on trombone the manager and Mack on trumpet the leader and Edmund Washington on clarinet and me on banjo

ctx.x: and I was telling you how I actually got to play banjo like my brother bought a banjo and I was teaching him and I finally he got discouraged and I started taking the banjo and well this fellow George Morris and Thomas Mack they were taking lessons from Mack with the trumpet player and Joy with the trombone player and I had another fellow named I believe his name was Edmund Washington taking Clannery a very good reading Clannery player mm-hmm well uh I used to go to their house in rehearsal you see and when they…

items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1979-12-05
items.q: And the saxophone player, Edmund Washington... they used to hire me... So we got this job... So this man came to the, and he decided to take us.

ctx.x: When did you start playing music professionally for, you know, your first few jobs?

Well I wasn't calling myself a professional before, before 24. I was in ninth grade, 35, right there, F1-0. And these two guys was taking lessons. This man and these guys were married men and everything. They left in the days first. The Trammer played George Morris, and Trump was played Thomas Mack. And the saxophone player, Edmund Washington. I just buried them this year, first part of this year. And they used to get a little job, they used to hire me. They had family and everything. I mean, they were work guys,…
Yeah. So you decided pretty much in Pensacola that, or?
